clue.text: Period clothes mostly embroidered, dressing two separately

indicators.note: embroidered cloth is worked over and rearranged, so these letters are reworked
dressing means wrapping round, so the reworked letters are arranged around the pair of numerals
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
two is the Roman numeral II, and separately says its two I's go in at different places

explanation.surface: A costume drama's period clothes, nearly all embroidered, are put on two actors one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' and 'dressing' shuffle the trimmed word with the two I's; 'separately' warns that the I's end up apart rather than side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eolithic is the early Stone Age era of crude flint tools, so it names a prehistoric period.

clue.text: Engraves swallows in elaborate scene

indicators.note: in places the swallowing word inside the reworked letters
elaborate, as a verb, means to work up or rework, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to have food is to swallow it, so swallows gives HAS

explanation.surface: An artist cuts a scene of swallows into metal in elaborate detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' looks like birds in the scene, but it is the verb 'has'; 'elaborate' gives ENCES, which takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchase is to engrave or chase ornamental patterns into metal, a synonym of engrave.

clue.text: Electronic playing facility rock 'n' roller built

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth who danced to rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: An arcade with electronic games for a rock 'n' roll fan has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British park with pitches; Teddy boys were 1950s rock 'n' roll fans in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erected has been put up or constructed, so it is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Middle of emmental portion served up to catch vermin?

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the cheese name
in a down clue served up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: A slice from the middle of an emmental is served, perhaps to lure a mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair of EMMENTAL is EN; PART read upwards becomes TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare, and the question mark flags that a trap set for vermin is one example.

clue.text: European pair extremely joyous drinking vermouth and lemon — more than one

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, and a pair gives two of them

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the outer letters hold the drink
extremely takes the extreme, outermost letters of joyous

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it

explanation.surface: Two cheerful Europeans drink vermouth with a twist of lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lemon' in British slang is a fool, and the dash with 'more than one' says the definition is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Eejit is Irish and Scottish slang for an idiot, and a lemon is likewise a foolish person, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Junk on sale by river irks posh types

indicators.note: junk means scrap or wreck, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: to irk is to anger, so irks gives angers

explanation.surface: Riverside junk put up for sale annoys well-to-do locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' shuffles ON SALE into SLOANE. Sloane Rangers were the posh young set around Sloane Square in Chelsea, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloane Rangers are the stereotyped upper-class young people of west London, a byword for poshness.

clue.text: Activity and feature of adders? They make calculations

parts.note: sliding is the gliding movement a snake makes
adders are snakes, and snakes are covered in scales

explanation.surface: A riddle about what adders do and wear, with adders apparently being calculating machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adders' suggests adding machines, but here they are snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sliding scales set fees, taxes or wages by a formula that varies with some other figure, so they work out amounts.

clue.text: Entrepreneur on break working out, as part of a five-a-day regime?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: Alan Sugar is a famous British entrepreneur, host of The Apprentice
to break something is to snap it
PE, physical education, is exercise or working out

explanation.surface: A business tycoon takes a break from exercising as part of a healthy-eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is a British businessman known from The Apprentice. Five-a-day is the UK advice to eat five portions of fruit and vegetables daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar snap peas are a vegetable, so they count towards the recommended daily portions of produce.

clue.text: Gaelic woman's delight regularly apparent when receiving hat

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the picked letters hold the hat
regularly takes every other letter of delight

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A Scottish woman is visibly delighted whenever she is given a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of delight, and 'receiving' takes the hat inside them before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilidh is a Scottish Gaelic female name, the equivalent of Helen.

clue.text: Bearing first of children with Mike out of wedlock

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of children
out of means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: wedlock is marriage
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike's first child was born out of wedlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of wedlock' seems to mean illegitimate, but it says M leaves MARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing and carriage both mean the way a person holds and conducts themselves, their deportment.

clue.text: Behind loaf tin, a slice

indicators.note: a slice is a cut piece from within the words loaf tin, taking letters across the gap

explanation.surface: A slice of loaf left over at the back of a baking tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical word for at or towards the stern, the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Is the new crossing good for boats?

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the shuffled letters straddle the other piece
new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a newly built crossing is suitable for boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles IS THE into EIHTS, and 'crossing' puts it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing rowing boat crewed by eight oarsmen, so eights are boats, as in the Oxford Eights Week races.

clue.text: Former carriage, interior not given public appearance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the interior, its central letter, is left out of the word

parts.note: carriage is the way one holds oneself, one's posture

explanation.surface: An old horse-drawn carriage, with its inside missing, goes on public display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior not given' drops the T at the centre of POSTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is being shown publicly or getting publicity, such as media coverage.

clue.text: Killer in Worcs borders hiding

indicators.note: with its borders hidden the word loses its outside letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A murderer is lying low in the border country of Worcestershire.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a killer whale or orca, and also a murderous monster in fantasy fiction.

clue.text: Margaret misses initial lodging because that's warmer at breakfast-time?

indicators.note: lodging means staying inside, so the other piece is placed within
missing its initial means the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Peggy is a pet form of the name Margaret
cos is an informal short form of because

explanation.surface: Margaret skips the first part of her stay because it is warmer at breakfast-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodging' looks like accommodation in the surface but is the insertion signal; the question mark marks the definition as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cosy is a small knitted or padded cover that keeps a boiled egg warm on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Approved of Kelvin disrupting party revolutionary

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into, so the unit goes inside
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Kelvin is approved of for disrupting a revolutionary party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DO into OD, and 'disrupting' puts K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: OK'd is the informal past tense of to OK, meaning sanctioned or given the go-ahead.

clue.text: Protective preparation made by civil engineer guarding home when on holiday

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: vac, short for vacation, is a holiday

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A civil engineer protects his house while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' puts home inside the engineer, and 'when on' sets that after the holiday in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine is a preparation given to protect against a disease, by building immunity.

clue.text: Feeling mushy peas around cold room above Iceland, say

parts.note: an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of mystery

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the other piece
mushy means mashed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cook senses that mushy peas want a cold room, perhaps a freezer from the Iceland store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' shuffles PEAS into SPAE, which goes 'around' C. Iceland is also a British frozen-food chain, but here it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the sky above a country, under that nation's control, so the space over Iceland is one example.

clue.text: Match during competition that is a favourite?

indicators.note: during means within, so the match goes inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a competition, such as the FA Cup
a tie is a match in a knockout cup

explanation.surface: A match in a cup competition: is one side the favourite?
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a single match in a British knockout cup competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie-pie is an endearing person, a darling or pet, so a favourite in the affectionate sense.

clue.text: Perhaps pond-life seem to incite pub brouhaha, all ending in casualty

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the other piece

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is the casualty department of a British hospital

indicators.note: all ending takes the final letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Pond-life seem to start a pub brawl, which all ends up in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pond-life' looks like an insult to the brawlers but is the definition; 'casualty' is the British hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoebae are single-celled organisms that live in fresh water, so they are an example of pond-life.

clue.text: Doc with meter reviewed layer of embryo

indicators.note: reviewed means looked over again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor looks over an embryo's development together with a measuring instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' shuffles DOC and METER together.
explanation.definitionFit: The ectoderm is the outermost of the three germ layers in an early embryo, which forms the skin and nerves.

clue.text: Obscure old film on teeth student ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: plaque is the bacterial film that forms on teeth
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A dentist ignores a student's question about an obscure old film on teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie, but it is a coating; 'ignored' drops L from PLAQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque is not transparent, and figuratively hard to understand, so obscure fits both ways.

clue.text: One moving overseas record company erected work unit

parts.note: EMI is a well-known British record company

indicators.note: in a down clue erected means set upright, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A record company's emigrant boss put up a new factory unit abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns ERG upside down in this down clue, giving GRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is a person who has left their own country to live in another, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Opening with Ron's car key again

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: Ron opens up with his car key once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a car key in the surface, but here it means type on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To key is to type text, so keying again is typing it out a second time.

clue.text: Amount of weight seaman's carrying variable

definitions.note: a measure of weight, given as a plural abbreviation

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the letters go round the other piece

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman, the 's being part of the surface
Z is a letter used for a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A sailor carries a variable weight of cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is an ordinary seaman, and algebra uses Z for an unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozs is the plural abbreviation of ounces, units in which an amount of weight is measured.

clue.text: Crystalline rock in wagon procured by pick

indicators.note: procured by means held within, so the wagon is taken inside the other piece

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best, the elite
a van is a covered wagon

explanation.surface: Rock in a wagon was dug out with a pickaxe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick' suggests a pickaxe, but it means the choicest of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvanite, or elvan, is a Cornish quartz-porphyry, a crystalline igneous rock.

clue.text: Bird's training collie latterly to pen sheep

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so these letters go round the animal

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training

indicators.note: latterly takes the last letter of collie

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A bird watches a collie being trained to pen sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pen' puts the sheep inside the training plus the collie's last letter, just before that final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Peewee is a dialect name for the lapwing, a bird named for its call.

clue.text: Attendant with historical records (five lost) for certain governments

parts.note: a squire was a knight's attendant

indicators.note: lost means the numeral is dropped from the word

parts.note: archives are historical records
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An aide finds some old records lost, affecting certain administrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops V, Roman five, from ARCHIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirearchy is rule by landed gentry, the squires, so squirearchies are kinds of government by that class.
